floor_history.headline: _exeque written in pure C for the first time (was INCLUDE_ASM, floor 187) using the already-merged GpuQueueItem struct; found+fixed a genuine missing extern (D_8009BF84) that was silently miscompiled;
Structural session dropped _exeque from floor 15 to 12: pre-computing a pointer to D_8009BE7C closed the final-callback block byte-exact; the triple-store residual survives two more reordering probes

Floor held at 12/187; exhausted pure-C respelling of the triple-store block (5 measured spellings, all byte-identical) and traced the exact rank_for_schedule LUID tie with the instrumented cc1's BB2_R
Directed permuter campaigns dropped _exeque's honest floor 12 -> 2/187 via two SOTN-sanctioned do-while(0) wraps (single-level around the triple-store block, then nested around its first two stores);

_exeque held at floor 2/187 (s4's do-while(0) chassis re-confirmed); s5 permuter session KILLED two hand-derived structural variants of the final-callback block and pushed the jalr-delay-slot permuter
Floor held at 2/187 (s4/s5 chassis re-confirmed); s6 structural session killed 4 fresh local respellings around the jalr-delay-slot residual, none closing or improving it.

frontier.hypothesis: The floor-2 residual (final-callback jalr delay-slot fill) is the SAME site s2's H6 found closable only via `volatile s32 *p` -- an IRQ-callback-installed function's own single-read test-and-clear of a flag it owns could qualify as a fourth catalogued use-site shape under legitimate-volatile-interrupt-touched, closing the last 2 instructions with zero further search once ruled on.
frontier.mechanism: policy/ruling question, not a GCC pass
frontier.next_probe: File a ruling-request citing memory/grind/_exeque/rejected/volatile-D_8009BE7C-guard-clear.c, hypotheses.md H6, src/display.c's DMACallback(2, _exeque) IRQ-install site, and the fact that the floor has been flat at 2/187 for three consecutive sessions (s4/s5/s6) across permuter (~24k iterations) and structural (this session's four probes) modalities with zero improvement found by any non-volatile lever.

frontier.hypothesis: A non-volatile pure-C lever for the jalr-delay-slot fill may still exist in a region this session and s4/s5 have not yet tried: restructuring how the STORE's address is materialized (e.g. a struct/field-access spelling of D_8009BE7C instead of a raw pointer local) so the compiler picks a different hard register for the address, one that DOES conflict with the call_insn's resource footprint.
frontier.mechanism: GCC 2.7.2 reorg.c mark_set_resources/mark_referenced_resources (called from fill_simple_delay_slots) computes conflicts between the trial insn's used/set hard registers and the call_insn's own resource set; if the store's address register happened to be one the call_insn's resource set includes (e.g. a return-value or argument register), the fill would be excluded
frontier.next_probe: Read tools/gcc-2.7.2/reorg.c's mark_set_resources for CALL_INSN (~reorg.c:3072-3079) to enumerate exactly which hard regs a MIPS call_insn's resource set includes, then try C-level spellings of the final block designed to force the store's address into one of those specific registers (e.g. introducing an intervening call-adjacent read that pressures register allocation) rather than random reordering.

frontier.hypothesis: The do-while(0)-wrapped chassis in candidate.c (unchanged since s4, re-confirmed s5 and this session) remains the best known starting point for any future session -- re-deriving it would waste a session, and this session's four new negative structural probes (all reverted, all banked as rejected/) further narrow what's worth trying: local statement/operand reordering in the final-block/outer-guard/SetIntrMask region is now measured exhausted across 7 distinct spellings (3 from s2/s4, 4 from this session) with zero improvements.
frontier.next_probe: Next session should apply memory/grind/_exeque/candidate.c verbatim (sandbox floor 2/187, re-confirmed this session), then EITHER file the ruling-request above OR pursue the reorg.c resource-set-targeted register-forcing probe (frontier item 2) -- a genuinely new axis, not another reordering variant.
